title: Private PoC weekly check-in — Observability minimum pack install + signal validation
next_steps: Redwood to provide a patched PrometheusRule bundle (or overlay) that avoids promtool parse failures in customer Prometheus version
Customer to change Vector/Fluent Bit buffering settings and validate SIEM forwarding end-to-end under load
Redwood to share the supported signal validation checklist and align on go-live pass/fail criteria
Schedule a 60-min live session to run the installer validation command and review dashboards together
action_items: Bruno Silva: send a minimal hotfix / workaround for the alert rule parsing error (promtool) and confirm compatibility with Prometheus 2.43 (due 2025-02-21)
Allison Grant: share recommended default alert group toggles + noise tuning guidance for PoC (due 2025-02-21)
Dev Patel: provide Support runbook snippet for 'rules not loaded after upgrade' incl. common RBAC causes (due 2025-02-24)
Liam O'Rourke: email customer the install guide link + values.yaml examples for customer-managed Grafana and datasource auth (due 2025-02-20)
Northbridge (Miguel/Jordan): raise Vector memory/disk buffers and enable file-based persistence; re-test log drop rate during load test (due 2025-02-23)
Northbridge (Priya): confirm whether SIEM endpoint requires mTLS client certs and provide CA chain requirements to Redwood (due 2025-02-20)
body:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Private PoC weekly check-in — Observability minimum pack install + signal validation
Recorded: 2025-02-19 17:00 UTC
Duration: 41 min

Attendees
Redwood Inference: Liam O'Rourke, Markus Klein, Bruno Silva, Allison Grant, Dev Patel
Northbridge Health Systems: Ava Chen, Miguel Santos, Priya Deshmukh, Jordan Lee

---
Summary (auto-generated)
- Team reviewed status of the Private observability minimum pack install in the on-prem PoC cluster.
- Customer reported two blockers: Prometheus rule parsing failures after upgrade and dropped logs forwarding to SIEM during peak traffic.
- Redwood proposed a short-term workaround (disable one rule group / apply overlay) and a medium-term fix (rule bundle compatibility + CI matrix).
- Next steps defined around validation command output, buffering configuration for log collector, and security requirements for SIEM (mTLS).

Topics
- PrometheusRule loading failures (promtool parse errors)
- Grafana provisioning + RBAC/service account scope
- Log pipeline drops to SIEM (Vector vs Fluent Bit, backpressure)
- “Supported signals” validation checklist for go-live

Questions (auto-generated)
- Which Prometheus version is running in the on-prem cluster, and is it pinned?
- Are we forwarding logs over TLS only or mutual TLS to the SIEM collector?
- Do you want default burn-rate alerts enabled in PoC, or keep them mostly off and use dashboards first?

---
Transcript

[00:00] Liam O'Rourke: Alright, hi everyone. Thanks for joining. This is our weekly PoC check-in. Goal today is just get a readout: install status of the minimum observability pack, any blockers, and agree on actions so we can get to the supported-signals validation.

[00:18] Ava Chen: Sounds good.

[00:20] Markus Klein: Hey all.

[00:22] Bruno Silva: Hi.

[00:23] Allison Grant: Hello.

[00:24] Dev Patel: Hi everyone.

[00:27] Liam O'Rourke: Ava, do you want to start? Last time we were mid-install on the on-prem cluster, and we were going to try the air-gapped bundle path.

[00:37] Ava Chen: Yep. So, good news: we did get the pack installed using the offline bundle. The installer picked up the artifact path okay once we corrected the directory layout. But we have two issues.

[00:49] Ava Chen: One is Prometheus rules. After we applied the PrometheusRule CRDs, Prometheus is rejecting one group, and then it seems like none of the groups load, which means no alerts.

[01:01] Ava Chen: Second is logs. We’re forwarding gateway and runtime logs to our SIEM collector and we’re seeing like… gaps. During the load test it’s pretty noticeable. We also see Vector complaining about retries.

[01:14] Liam O'Rourke: Okay. That matches the email thread. Let’s do rules first. Miguel, you had the exact error, right?

[01:21] Miguel Santos: Yeah. I can paste it here but basically promtool, or Prometheus, says “error parsing rules, unexpected character” and it points to a line with like a label matcher.

[01:33] Miguel Santos: The snippet is: `sum by (route) (rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))` and it complains near the regex quotes. Which is weird because it’s normal PromQL. But I wonder if it’s our Prometheus version.

[01:52] Bruno Silva: Do you know which Prometheus you’re running?

[01:55] Jordan Lee: It’s… hold on… 2.43 in the cluster. We’re not on the newest. We pinned it because of another dependency.

[02:03] Bruno Silva: Okay, that’s helpful. We test against 2.48 and 2.49 internally, and we should be backwards compatible, but we’ve seen older promtool be picky with escaping inside YAML when it goes through Helm templating.

[02:18] Allison Grant: Another angle: are you using Prometheus Operator to load PrometheusRule, or plain Prometheus with rule_files? Because the operator can reject if the rule YAML is not exactly what it expects.

[02:28] Jordan Lee: Operator. kube-prometheus-stack.

[02:31] Allison Grant: Got it.

[02:34] Miguel Santos: The other thing is when one group fails, it looks like the operator says “rules failed to sync” and then none of them are active. So we lose the whole bundle.

[02:45] Dev Patel: That behavior is consistent. We’ve seen tickets where one invalid rule prevents the operator from applying the ConfigMap, so it’s all-or-nothing. We want to avoid that.

[02:56] Liam O'Rourke: Bruno, do we have a known workaround? Like disable a group?

[03:00] Bruno Silva: Yes. We have rule groups split: SLO burn, pipeline health, resource exhaustion, and “missing signals”. We can give you a values toggle to disable the group that’s failing, but first we should identify the exact rule.

[03:13] Miguel Santos: It pointed to the burn-rate group. The rule name is something like “GatewayAvailabilityBurn”. I can’t remember exact.

[03:20] Allison Grant: That one uses multi-window, multi-burn logic with `for` and sometimes additional label joins. If the operator is old, it might not like some YAML formatting too.

[03:32] Bruno Silva: Can you share the rendered YAML? Not the template, the rendered PrometheusRule object from the cluster.

[03:38] Jordan Lee: Yeah, we can `kubectl get prometheusrule ... -o yaml`.

[03:42] Liam O'Rourke: Let’s do it now if that’s easy.

[03:44] Jordan Lee: Sure, give me a sec.

[03:49] (pause)

[04:02] Jordan Lee: Okay I’m looking at it. There’s a line that has `status=~"5.."` but in YAML it’s… it’s double escaped. It shows `status=~\"5..\"` inside the string.

[04:15] Bruno Silva: Aha. That’s likely it. It means Helm is escaping and then the operator escapes again, or something in your pipeline is injecting extra slashes.

[04:23] Miguel Santos: We are using ArgoCD with Helm. And we have a values file that does some string substitution, but not there I think.

[04:30] Bruno Silva: The rule expressions should not contain escaped quotes like that, it should be just `status=~"5.."` in the final YAML string (or single quotes around the whole expression). If it’s `\"`, promtool might choke.

[04:44] Allison Grant: We can avoid quotes entirely by using single quotes for the YAML string and keep the regex quotes normal, or use `{status=~"5.."}` inside single-quoted YAML. That tends to be robust.

[04:55] Ava Chen: So is that on you or on us?

[04:57] Bruno Silva: Could be both. Our chart should render in a safe way, independent of tool chain. If it’s coming from our chart, we fix. If it’s coming from your overlay tooling, we can give a recommended patch.

[05:10] Liam O'Rourke: For the PoC timeline, we probably want the short-term workaround: toggle burn-rate group off so at least the rest loads and dashboards work, while we get a patched bundle.

[05:22] Miguel Santos: That’d be fine. For PoC we mostly wanted dashboards and a couple critical alerts, not paging us.

[05:28] Allison Grant: That’s consistent with our philosophy. In a PoC, enable the critical availability and pipeline health alerts, keep SLO burns disabled unless you’re ready.

[05:39] Dev Patel: Also, in case it helps, we have a runbook for “rules not loaded” that basically says: check `prometheus-operator` logs for parse errors, validate rule with `promtool check rules`, and confirm RBAC for reading the PrometheusRule resources.

[05:54] Priya Deshmukh: On RBAC, we saw Grafana provisioning fail the first time because the service account didn’t have permission to list ConfigMaps in the monitoring namespace.

[06:03] Ava Chen: Yeah we fixed that by granting get/list on ConfigMaps. But we’re cautious about widening it.

[06:10] Allison Grant: That’s reasonable. For the minimum pack we aim for least-privilege. For Grafana provisioning, we can scope to the namespace and to the specific label selectors. But in Kubernetes RBAC you can’t fully restrict to a label, so it becomes namespace + resource type.

[06:26] Priya Deshmukh: Right, that’s what our security review flagged.

[06:29] Liam O'Rourke: We can capture that as a follow-up. But I want to make sure you have dashboards showing data now?

[06:35] Miguel Santos: Partially. The gateway dashboard shows RPS and latency. The runtime dashboard shows some panels but others are blank. KV cache hit rate is blank. And the “queue depth” panel is blank.

[06:48] Allison Grant: That could be missing metrics. Are you scraping the runtime metrics endpoint? And is the runtime version the one that includes the new labels?

[06:57] Jordan Lee: We’re scraping. Metrics are there. But I noticed the labels are different: it’s `model_name` not `model`, and `route_id` not `route`.

[07:07] Bruno Silva: Hmm. The pack expects `model` and `route` labels in some dashboards, but we also tried to be flexible. If you’re on an older core, that mismatch will cause empty panels.

[07:18] Ava Chen: We’re on the private build from like three weeks ago. We didn’t take the very latest image because we were stabilizing.

[07:25] Liam O'Rourke: Okay. That’s a known integration point: the metrics contract. In the min pack project we added guardrails and normalized label names.

[07:33] Allison Grant: We can give you a dashboard variant that uses your existing labels, but longer-term you’ll want the normalized labels so your dashboards match supported baseline.

[07:42] Miguel Santos: Yeah, for PoC I just need something that works. But I’m okay updating if you have a recommended build.

[07:48] Markus Klein: From a deployment standpoint, it’s usually easier to update Redwood core than carry a custom dashboard fork. Less drift.

[07:56] Ava Chen: Makes sense.

[07:58] Liam O'Rourke: Let’s park that for a second and go to the logs dropping issue, because that sounds operationally worse.

[08:05] Miguel Santos: So, we are using Vector as the daemonset. We take container logs from the gateway and runtime pods, transform to JSON, and forward over TLS to our SIEM ingest endpoint.

[08:18] Miguel Santos: Under load, Vector reports “sink request failed” and “buffer full” and then we see dropped events.

[08:26] Priya Deshmukh: And our SIEM team is asking: are you sampling? Are you redacting? And do we have mTLS? Currently it’s TLS but no client cert.

[08:35] Dev Patel: Our default is TLS with server validation. mTLS is supported but requires you to configure the collector with client certs and mount secrets.

[08:45] Bruno Silva: Also, log drops can be because the SIEM endpoint is rate limiting. Do you have any response codes?

[08:52] Miguel Santos: Mostly 429s and some 503s.

[08:56] Allison Grant: That’s backpressure. You need buffering, retries with jitter, and possibly a local disk buffer for on-prem. Memory-only buffers will drop.

[09:06] Jordan Lee: We set buffer to 512MB. No disk buffer currently.

[09:12] Markus Klein: For on-prem, especially if the SIEM has maintenance windows, we strongly recommend disk-based buffering.

[09:19] Ava Chen: Our cluster nodes have limited local disk. But we can provision a hostPath to a dedicated partition.

[09:26] Liam O'Rourke: Can you quantify the loss? Like what percent events?

[09:30] Miguel Santos: During a 20-minute load test, we estimate around 8-12% missing based on request_id correlation. Not perfect but significant.

[09:41] Dev Patel: That’s enough to make incident triage annoying.

[09:44] Allison Grant: Are you sampling debug logs? Some of the runtime logs can be very chatty if debug is on.

[09:50] Jordan Lee: Debug is off. But we do log request completion lines for every request.

[09:56] Bruno Silva: You can change that to sample successes and keep full fidelity for errors. Our defaults recommend: always keep error logs, sample 1-5% of successful request logs, and keep aggregate metrics for everything.

[10:10] Miguel Santos: We can do that. Our SIEM team actually prefers fewer events with consistent fields.

[10:16] Priya Deshmukh: And redaction is important. We can’t ship prompts or responses.

[10:20] Bruno Silva: Right. The structured logs in Redwood are designed to avoid content by default. Fields like request_id, tenant, model, route, status_code, error_code, latency_ms. No payload.

[10:32] Priya Deshmukh: Okay. But we did see some logs with “prompt_len” and “top_p” and stuff. That’s fine.

[10:38] Allison Grant: That’s safe.

[10:40] Liam O'Rourke: So action wise: Miguel/Jordan, you’ll increase Vector buffer and enable disk buffer persistence, and implement sampling for non-error success logs.

[10:52] Miguel Santos: Yes.

[10:53] Jordan Lee: Yes.

[10:54] Liam O'Rourke: Priya, you’ll confirm if SIEM requires mTLS.

[10:58] Priya Deshmukh: Yep.

[11:00] Liam O'Rourke: Redwood side, we can send you the recommended Vector config snippet with disk buffer and sampling filter.

[11:06] Dev Patel: I can pull what we’ve used on another regulated on-prem install.

[11:10] Markus Klein: We also should confirm that you’re not double-encoding JSON. That can inflate payload sizes.

[11:17] Miguel Santos: We might be. We have a transform stage that wraps as JSON string again.

[11:23] Bruno Silva: That could increase the bytes and hit rate limits sooner.

[11:27] Ava Chen: Okay.

[11:29] Liam O'Rourke: Back to dashboards and missing panels. Allison, can you outline what “supported signals” means for this PoC? Just so we agree on pass/fail.

[11:39] Allison Grant: Sure. For us, minimum supported means: (1) gateway metrics: request rate, error rate, latency percentiles; (2) runtime metrics: prefill vs decode time, queue depth, batch size, GPU utilization; (3) control plane health basic; and (4) pipeline health for metrics and logs. Plus, cardinality constraints: we need model + route labels but not arbitrary user IDs.

[12:03] Allison Grant: In your case, the dashboards being blank indicates either metrics missing or labels mismatched. We can run the installer validation command, which checks endpoints and also runs a couple of PromQL queries that should return non-empty.

[12:18] Jordan Lee: We haven’t run that. We saw the CLI command but didn’t do it.

[12:22] Bruno Silva: The command is `redwood-private validate observability` in the newer installer. Not sure which version you have.

[12:29] Ava Chen: We’re on installer 0.19.2.

[12:33] Bruno Silva: Validation command landed in 0.20.x. We can either upgrade the installer or I can send the standalone script version.

[12:42] Ava Chen: Upgrading installer is a little scary because of the air-gap. But we can do it if it’s just swapping the binary.

[12:48] Markus Klein: Usually it’s fine; but we can do it in a maintenance window. Alternative: run our checklist manually.

[12:56] Liam O'Rourke: Given timeline, I’d propose: Bruno sends the standalone validation steps today or tomorrow. Then schedule a live session next week where we run through it.

[13:08] Ava Chen: Okay.

[13:10] Priya Deshmukh: Also, question: are you expecting us to run Grafana ourselves? We already have a Grafana cluster. We don’t want another.

[13:18] Liam O'Rourke: The min pack supports customer-managed Grafana and Prometheus. We can provision dashboards into your existing Grafana via API or provisioning ConfigMaps depending on how you run it.

[13:30] Allison Grant: For on-prem, we often do provisioning via ConfigMaps in the Grafana namespace, but if you have a separate Grafana, we can export dashboards as JSON and you import them, or we use a service account token.

[13:42] Priya Deshmukh: We’d prefer import via API with a service account that has minimal permissions.

[13:47] Dev Patel: Grafana permissions get tricky. Service account needs folder write access. But we can scope it to a folder.

[13:55] Miguel Santos: We created a folder “Redwood-Private” and gave a service account editor there.

[14:02] Allison Grant: That should work.

[14:04] Liam O'Rourke: Okay. Now, the rules parsing issue: Bruno, you’ll produce a patch that avoids the double-escaping in rendered YAML and confirm with Prometheus 2.43.

[14:14] Bruno Silva: Yes. I’ll do two things: (1) provide a values toggle to disable the burn-rate group for immediate unblocking; (2) send a patched rule file with expressions single-quoted and no extra escaping, plus a note for Helm/Argo.

[14:31] Ava Chen: Great.

[14:33] Miguel Santos: Quick question: even if we disable burn-rate, will we still get “pipeline health” alerts? Those are useful.

[14:40] Allison Grant: Yes. Pipeline health is separate group. That includes collector backlog/drops and “missing metrics” sentinel.

[14:47] Miguel Santos: Perfect.

[14:49] Dev Patel: Just to manage expectations: in PoC we should keep paging disabled. We can route alerts to a Slack channel or email.

[14:56] Ava Chen: Agreed.

[14:58] Liam O'Rourke: Any other issues? Anything about GPU dashboard?

[15:03] Jordan Lee: GPU dashboard shows utilization, but memory is blank. We’re on NVIDIA A10. Node exporter is there.

[15:11] Allison Grant: GPU memory comes from DCGM exporter usually. Are you running it?

[15:15] Jordan Lee: We are not.

[15:18] Markus Klein: That’s a common miss. In air-gapped installs, DCGM exporter image needs mirroring too.

[15:25] Ava Chen: We can mirror it. But we need the exact image digest.

[15:29] Bruno Silva: We can provide pinned image references as part of the offline bundle. If it’s not included in your current bundle, we’ll add it.

[15:39] Liam O'Rourke: Noted. That’s important for the “day-1 usable” requirement.

[15:45] Priya Deshmukh: On images, we need to run them through internal scanning. If you can provide a list of images + SHA, that helps.

[15:52] Markus Klein: We can provide a manifest list.

[15:56] Liam O'Rourke: Great.

[16:00] Miguel Santos: One more: the gateway dashboard has a panel “stream disconnects” or something, it’s always zero. We do streaming responses.

[16:09] Allison Grant: That metric might require the newer gateway build. It was added recently. If you’re on older, it’ll be missing.

[16:17] Miguel Santos: Okay.

[16:18] Liam O'Rourke: So that’s consistent with the label mismatch discussion. We’ll align on a recommended Redwood core version for PoC.

[16:26] Markus Klein: Ava, are you okay taking an updated core image in the PoC? We can stage it.

[16:32] Ava Chen: Yes, but we need it in the offline registry with a changelog. And we need to validate nothing changes in outputs.

[16:41] Liam O'Rourke: Totally. We can keep it to instrumentation changes, no model/runtime behavior changes. But we’ll document.

[16:48] Bruno Silva: Instrumentation changes should be safe, but I’ll confirm.

[16:51] Dev Patel: From supportability angle, the closer you are to the baseline metrics contract, the easier it is to support.

[16:58] Ava Chen: Understood.

[17:01] Liam O'Rourke: Let’s do a quick recap of decisions and next steps.

[17:06] Liam O'Rourke: One, rules parsing: Bruno sends workaround + patch and confirms with Prometheus 2.43.

[17:12] Bruno Silva: Yes.

[17:13] Liam O'Rourke: Two, logs: Northbridge updates Vector buffering (disk persistence) and sampling for success logs; Redwood sends config snippet.

[17:22] Miguel Santos: Yes.

[17:23] Dev Patel: Yes.

[17:24] Liam O'Rourke: Three, missing dashboard panels: likely label mismatch / missing metrics; Redwood to recommend core build, and we run validation checklist together next week.

[17:33] Allison Grant: Yes.

[17:34] Ava Chen: Works.

[17:36] Liam O'Rourke: Four, GPU memory panels require DCGM exporter; Redwood provides pinned image list and adds to offline bundle manifest.

[17:44] Markus Klein: Yup.

[17:46] Priya Deshmukh: And I’ll confirm mTLS requirements with SIEM team.

[17:50] Liam O'Rourke: Great.

[17:52] (conversation continues with details)

[18:00] Ava Chen: Can I ask about retention? We’re keeping Prometheus for 15 days only. Is that enough for your alerts?

[18:07] Allison Grant: For burn-rate alerts, we need multi-window but it’s in hours/days, typically 2h, 6h, 1d, 3d windows. If you only keep 15 days, that’s fine. We’re not doing 30/90-day analytics in the min pack.

[18:23] Miguel Santos: Okay.

[18:25] Priya Deshmukh: For logs, we keep in SIEM for 1 year.

[18:28] Dev Patel: That’s on your side; we don’t require us to store it.

[18:32] Liam O'Rourke: That’s aligned.

[18:35] Jordan Lee: Another question: Do you support Grafana Cloud? Not for us, but for future.

[18:41] Liam O'Rourke: For Private minimum pack, we target standard components. In air-gapped, Grafana Cloud is usually not feasible. In VPC deployments, some customers do use managed services; we can discuss later.

[18:54] Ava Chen: Okay.

[18:56] Miguel Santos: I did want to mention, we evaluated Datadog for this but it’s not allowed on-prem. That’s why we’re doing this with Prometheus and SIEM.

[19:05] Liam O'Rourke: Makes sense.

[19:07] Markus Klein: Also many of our Private customers use Elastic, Splunk, things like that. We aim to forward structured logs.

[19:15] Priya Deshmukh: We’re on Elastic, but with an internal front door.

[19:18] Bruno Silva: That explains the 429s.

[19:21] Miguel Santos: Yeah.

[19:23] Liam O'Rourke: Before we close, can we agree on the live validation session time?

[19:28] Ava Chen: Next Tuesday same time works.

[19:31] Liam O'Rourke: Perfect. I’ll send an invite.

[19:34] Dev Patel: And for the immediate fix, if you disable the burn-rate group, you should see the rest of the rules load. If they still don’t, we may have a second issue.

[19:44] Miguel Santos: Okay.

[19:45] Allison Grant: If you can also check operator logs after you apply, that would be good. And run `promtool check rules` on the rendered file, just to confirm.

[19:54] Jordan Lee: Will do.

[19:57] Liam O'Rourke: Anything else we missed?

[20:00] Ava Chen: No, this was helpful.

[20:02] Priya Deshmukh: Good.

[20:03] Miguel Santos: Thanks.

[20:04] Liam O'Rourke: Great, thanks all. We’ll follow up with the patch and config snippets, and see you Tuesday.

---
End of transcript

Notes
- Some speaker attribution may be inaccurate due to transcription.
- Technical terms (PrometheusRule, promtool, Vector) captured as heard.
